transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start time: 14:30 EST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Cedarbridge - Head Infra), Evan Riley (Cedarbridge - Security Architect), Sofia Martinez (Cedarbridge - DevOps), Tom Blake (Cedarbridge - Legal)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on access controls, key management (BYOK/HSM), audit log retention/export, and deployment modality (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is evaluating for POC in Q1 2027, regulatory constraints for EU data residency and long-term retention for finance records.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from Redwood, luis is my solutions engineer. can we do a quick round robin for roles?
[00:12] Priya Nair: sure i'm priya, head of infra at cedarbridge, we run hybrid cloud, mostly aws eu-west for sensitive workloads.
[00:18] Evan Riley: evan, security architect; i'm focused on access controls, retention policy and KMS.
[00:23] Sofia Martinez: sofia, devops, i'll be hands-on for any private deployment.
[00:27] Tom Blake: tom from legal, i'll be checking retention and e-discovery questions.
[00:31] Luis Ortega: great, thanks. i'll be doing the technical parts; quick agenda, we'll cover SOC2/ISO status, sso/scim, rbac mapping, audit logs, k m s options and the three deployment modes. sound good?
[00:44] Priya Nair: yep let's go. we have a vague timeline - want to start a POC early jan - decision by end of feb. security is biggest gating factor.

[01:05] Maya Chen: high level -- redwood's typical enterprise flow: hosted api for fast dev, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, and private deployment for air-gapped or strict network controls. we can walk through how each handles keys, logs, and sso.

[01:28] Evan Riley: first question - soc2 and iso. do you have certs? and is the scope the hosted service only, or do you include dedicated/private under the same program?
[01:40] Maya Chen: good q. we maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 for the control plane and hosted service. dedicated is offered under contractual commitments and is covered by the dedicated SLA - essentially the controls extend but customers with dedicated reserved capacity often require an addendum; private deployments rely on customer-managed infrastructure so they are outside of our hosted audit scope, but we provide a private deployment attestation and a deployment-runbook to assist audits. i'll send the certs after this meeting.
[02:10] Priya Nair: so private is out of scope for your SOC2, you don't audit our environment obviously. we expected that. we just need the runbook and any baseline controls.
[02:21] Luis Ortega: yes exactly; for private you get the software and the control plane handshake, but logs and key custody live with you. for dedicated we keep tenant-level logs and we can include them in the SOC2 evidence pack.

[02:40] Tom Blake: retention — regulator requires seven years for some financial artifacts. how do you support long-term retention of logs and outputs?
[02:49] Maya Chen: two pieces - audit logs and user data. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via streaming (we support S3, Kafka, and syslog forwarders) and retention is fully customer-controlled on your side; redwood also keeps operational audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted, longer with enterprise retention add-on. for model outputs or transcripts, we have configurable retention policies per-tenant; hosted default is 30 days but we can extend to match your retention SLAs under contract.
[03:20] Evan Riley: do you offer write-once immutable logs or WORM for compliance?
[03:25] Luis Ortega: we can support immutable S3 buckets (object lock) when streaming logs to your account. for hosted-native storage we can enable append-only audit trails for critical events with longer retention, but true WORM long-term custody we recommend pushing to your storage.

[03:44] Priya Nair: KMS — important. can we bring our own key? HSM? who's the root of trust?
[03:51] Maya Chen: yes BYOK supported for hosted and dedicated. options: you can provide KMS keys in your cloud account (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we integrate via customer managed keys where secrets never leave your account. for higher assurance, we support HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM) and bring-your-own-HSM for private deployments. root of trust remains in your key material.
[04:15] Evan Riley: is there support for offline key rotation or split key custody?
[04:19] Luis Ortega: split custody is possible in the private model; for hosted/dedicated we support regular rotation and we can sign key material with customer HSM via external key encryption keys (EKKs). offline rotation workflows we can document — depends on your KMS provider.

[04:38] Sofia Martinez: on SSO, we use okta with SAML and SCIM for group provisioning. can we map Okta groups to RBAC roles in Redwood?
[04:46] Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user + group sync. you can map SAML attributes or SCIM groups to roles and apply least-privilege RBAC. we also support granular route-level permissions for model access and key operations visibility.
[05:05] Priya Nair: do you have org-level and project-level roles? our teams need separation so infra ops can't access PII-labeled prompts.
[05:12] Luis Ortega: we have org, project, and token-level controls. token-level scoping is important — you can create tokens limited to embeddings only or generation only, and enforce IP whitelists and network policy for those tokens.

[05:32] Evan Riley: audit logging: which events are logged? are prompt/response payloads logged?
[05:39] Maya Chen: event types: auth events (sso/login), admin changes (role change, key rotation), model invocation metadata (call id, latency, model version), runtime errors. By default full request/response payloads are retained for 30 days AND masked for PII if configured. for customers that require never storing full payloads, we offer a no-retain mode where payloads are streamed and not persisted in hosted storage — useful for high-sensitivity use cases.
[06:12] Tom Blake: masking is fine but legal wants auditability for e-discovery — if we mask, can we still retrieve originals under legal hold?
[06:18] Luis Ortega: in hosted we can enable encrypted long-term archives to your S3, key-controlled by you. retrieval can be gated via access control and audit trails. for private deployment originals remain in your environment so legal access is your process.

[06:36] Priya Nair: data residency — some datasets must stay in eu-west. can dedicated or hosted be region-locked?
[06:42] Maya Chen: yes, region pinning is available. hosted tenants can be provisioned in eu regions; dedicated capacity can be reserved in a region and traffic routed accordingly. private deployments run in your VPC so obviously reside where you deploy.

[07:00] Evan Riley: regulatory question — do you ever use customer data for model training?
[07:04] Maya Chen: we don't use customer prompts or outputs to train our models by default for enterprise customers. training or benchmarking with customer data is opt-in and contractual. i'll note that in the doc i'll send.

[07:17] Sofia Martinez: performance — if we go private on-prem with our GPU cluster, what's the latency delta vs hosted?
[07:23] Luis Ortega: depends on your network topology and model. private on-prem typically has lower intra-datacenter latency and gives you direct GPU access; hosted dedicated in-region is comparable. the biggest gains come from routing policies and cache locality — we can run a benchmark POC.

[07:46] Priya Nair: tokenization and data leakage — how do you prevent prompt data from leaking between tenants?
[07:52] Luis Ortega: multi-tenant isolation is enforced in the serving runtime; KV cache and prefix caches are per-tenant. for extra assurance we recommend dedicated capacity or private deployment which isolates processes and memory.

[08:08] Evan Riley: what about penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure?
[08:11] Maya Chen: we publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and have annual pen tests; we can share a summary and remediation timelines. for dedicated and private we support coordinate testing under NDA.

[08:27] Tom Blake: legal — any standard PDP/processing addendum for data processors?
[08:31] Maya Chen: yes we have DPA templates and standard contractual clauses for EU. we'll include the DPA and the deployment addendum in the packet.

[08:40] Priya Nair: network connectivity for private deployment — do you support air-gapped install, or just VPC peering?
[08:45] Luis Ortega: both. we offer a VPC deployment model where the control plane is managed and the runtime sits in your VPC. for higher-security customers we provide an on-prem bundle that can be installed air-gapped; deployment team supports the install, but logs and keys stay local.

[09:03] Evan Riley: monitoring and metrics — do you expose token-level billing and latency traces?
[09:08] Maya Chen: yes our console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and per-model traces. we also provide tracing hooks you can forward to your observability platform.

[09:22] Priya Nair: can audit logs be pushed in near-real time to our SIEM? we'd rather not poll S3.
[09:27] Luis Ortega: absolutely; we support streaming to Kafka or syslog collectors for near-real time ingestion to SIEM.

[09:40] Sofia Martinez: for SCIM provisioning, do you support group-to-role lifecycle (deprovision on group leave)?
[09:45] Maya Chen: yes deprovisioning via SCIM is supported. we also have an option to auto-disable active tokens on user deactivation.

[10:00] Evan Riley: encryption at rest — AES-256 ok? any FIPS validated modules?
[10:04] Luis Ortega: hosted storage uses AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit; we can operate in FIPS mode for enterprise customers and use FIPS-validated crypto libraries when requested.

[10:20] Priya Nair: ok sounds promising. as next steps, we'll need SOC2 and ISO docs, the private deployment checklist and an ops diagram, and sample SAML metadata.
[10:29] Maya Chen: noted. i'll package SOC2/ISO + DPA + deployment runbook. luis will prepare a benchmark plan and network diagram. we'll find a time jan 4-8 for the deep technical session.

[10:43] Tom Blake: one last question — model outputs: do you have controls to redact PII automatically?
[10:48] Luis Ortega: yes we have configurable PII detection and redaction pipelines and can apply it at ingestion or at storage. we'll include examples in the security whitepaper.

[10:59] Priya Nair: thanks everyone. that's the substance we needed.
[11:03] Maya Chen: thanks all, i'll follow up with the packet by friday (jan 2) and include contact for our deployment team.
[11:10] Evan Riley: thanks.
[11:12] Sofia Martinez: thanks.
[11:13] End of meeting.

Recap / explicit next steps (verbatim):
- Maya: send SOC2/ISO artifacts, security whitepaper, DPA and deployment runbook (target 2027-01-02).
- Luis: produce private deployment checklist, ops/network diagram, benchmark plan (target 2027-01-07).
- Evan: share SAML metadata, group mapping and retention requirements (target 2027-01-04).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: K M S sometimes transcribed as 'kay em ess', occasional overlap in speaker channels; filled pauses present.
